items.title: MCMC, Selangor to expand filtered internet service to public premises and private institutions, says exco
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Aug 23 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC), in collaboration with the Selangor state government, plans to expand its filtered internet service to public premises and private higher learning institutions (IPTS). He said content filtering was important to ensure digital access was not misused during important activities such as prayers and learning sessions. On cyber threats, Mohammad Fahmi said 35,073 online scam cases were recorded as of June, involving losses of RM951.7 million, with investment scams accounting for RM413.8 million.

items.title: Anti-illegal racing op on Linkedua nets 75 summonses, 31 motorcycles
items.summary: ISKANDAR PUTERI: Police issued 75 summonses and seized 31 motorcycles in an operation at the Malaysia-Singapore Second Link (Linkedua) early this morning after identifying illegal racing hotspots where motorcyclists would perform dangerous stunts and disturb public order. Acting district police chief superintendent Saifullah Jaya @ Yahaya said 50 motorcyclists and pillon riders - 48 men and two women, along with 42 motorcycles were checked during the operation from 1am to 4am. "Offences found included not having side mirrors, no registration plates, fancy registration plates that do not follow specifications, modifying the vehicle structure such as exhaust pipes, not having driving licence and insurance coverage.

items.title: Tesla to launch Cybercab robotaxi in Texas early September
items.summary: SAN FRANCISCO: US electric vehicle maker Tesla will launch its Cybercab robotaxi early September, reported Xinhua quoting a Tesla-focused news outlet Teslarati report. Tesla CEO Elon Musk has previously said the company plans to sell the Cybercab to private customers for less than US$30,000 apiece. First unveiled in October 2024, the Cybercab is central to Tesla's robotaxi ambitions.

items.title: Employer charged with harbouring 127 undocumented migrants
items.summary: PASIR MAS: A Malaysian employer was charged at the Sessions Court today with allowing 127 undocumented migrants to remain at a premises under his control in Sering, Kota Baru, on Aug 10. Nasrullah, from Jerteh, Terengganu, was charged under Section 55E(1) of the Immigration Act 1959/63. The charge stated that the 127 undocumented migrants had allegedly committed offences under Section 6(1)(c) and Section 15(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63 and Regulation 39(b) of the Immigration Regulations 1963.

items.title: Selangor may declare holiday if host contingent emerge overall Sukma champions, says exco
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 23 — The Selangor government will consider declaring an occasional holiday if the host contingent emerge overall champions at the ongoing Malaysia Games (SUKMA) 2026. State Youth, Sports and Entrepreneurship Committee chairman Mohd Najwan Halimi said the matter would only be announced after the medal tally is finalised, with the Selangor contingent looking well placed to end the Games on a high. Najwan said that as of 2.50 pm today, Selangor had collected 85 gold medals, with the latest contributed by, among others, the women’s Mobile Legends: Bang Bang (MLBB) esports team, women’s 3m springboard diving, women’s singles table tennis and men’s singles lawn bowls.

items.title: Got 20,000 tech engineers, but where are the investors? Jerejak may have the answer, says Bayan Baru MP
items.summary: Bayan Baru MP Sim Tze Tzin said the proposed 32-hectare development could bring venture capitalists, private equity firms, bankers and technology investors closer to the engineers driving Penang’s semiconductor industry, The Star reported. Sim said Penang has about 20,000 integrated circuit design engineers, many of whom remain salaried employees because they lack investors to help them establish their own companies. Sim, who lived in Silicon Valley for six years, said regular interaction between engineers, entrepreneurs and investors could help generate new ideas and spur the growth of Penang’s technology sector.

items.title: BN should stand on its own without treating rivals as enemies – Perak MCA
items.summary: IPOH: Barisan Nasional must be prepared to face the upcoming general election on its own without treating other political coalitions as enemies, says Perak MCA. Perak MCA chairman Datuk Dr Mah Hang Soon said voters must not be left confused about the values BN represents. "BN must maintain consistent, transparent, and explainable principles.

items.title: PM approves additional RM1m for Hindu crematorium project in Bagan, says PHEB
items.summary: BUTTERWORTH, Aug 23 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has approved an additional RM1 million allocation to the Penang State Hindu Endowments Board (PHEB) for the construction of a modern Hindu crematorium in Bagan here, said PHEB chairman RSN Rayer. He said the additional allocation brought the total funding for the project to RM2.5 million, up from the RM1.5 million previously approved by Anwar. He said the original RM1.5 million allocation was found to be insufficient to implement the project, which is much needed by the Hindu community, particularly in Seberang Perai.

items.title: FT Pas sets up 11 task forces for GE16
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Federal territories Pas will establish 11 specialised task forces - one for each of its policy offerings under its "Wilayah Sejahtera" vision - to develop concrete policies ahead of the 16th general election. FT Pas commissioner Azhar Yahya said the task forces, announced at the Federal Territories Pas Convention here today, would each comprise experts, professionals and technocrats relevant to their respective areas. He said the convention, held ahead of Pas Muktamar in September, adopted 12 resolutions under the Wilayah Sejahtera theme, with the 12th resolution being the formal commitment to establish the task forces.

items.title: 'I had only them in this world': Daughter mourns father, sisters killed in Immigration truck crash
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: "Let's eat. Those simple invitations from her father and two younger sisters are now painful memories for Siti Shakira, who lost all three when an Immigration Department truck ploughed into them at an intersection on Jalan Sultan Ismail here last Wednesday. Her father would often ask, "Along, let's eat", while her sister Siti Norshazlin would invite her to the night market and her youngest sister, Siti Darwisyah Auni, would ask her to buy her something.

items.title: VIP escorts must not come at the expense of road safety
items.summary: LETTERS: Sharanjit Singh's report in the New Sunday Times, titled 'Sirens On, Rules Off?' Sirens and flashing lights come suddenly from behind, with little warning. Some feel nervous every time they hear a siren.

items.title: Post-mortem shows 11-year-old tahfiz participant found in Lenggeng pond died from drowning, police say no signs of abuse
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 23 — An 11-year-old boy who was found in a pond near a foundation centre in Kampung Kapal, Lenggeng early today died from drowning, resulting in a lack of oxygen, police said. “External and internal examinations of the victim’s body also found no other injuries or signs indicating abuse,” the senior police officer was quoted as saying. The boy had been reported missing while taking part in a tahfiz – a Quran memorisation – programme before he was found in a weak condition in a pond near the site.

items.title: After southern Thailand blasts, Wisma Putra tells Malaysians to think twice before crossing border
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 23 — Malaysians planning to travel to or cross into southern Thailand have been urged to exercise heightened caution and postpone non-essential trips following a wave of bomb blasts and other attacks across the region last night. The Foreign Ministry, also called Wisma Putra, said no Malaysians had been reported affected by the incidents in Yala, Pattani and Narathiwat, but advised those residing in, travelling through or planning trips to the affected areas to remain vigilant and follow local security instructions. “Malaysians residing in, travelling through, or intending to travel to and from the southern border provinces of Thailand are strongly advised to exercise heightened caution, remain vigilant, and strictly observe all safety advisories, curfews, and security instructions implemented by local authorities,” it said in a media advisory today.

items.title: 51 incidents reported in southern Thailand including IED attacks
items.summary: According to an update issued by the Internal Security Operations Command Region 4 (ISOC 4), the incidents were reported in 12 areas across Narathiwat, Pattani and Yala from about 8pm. The spokesman said Narathiwat recorded the highest number of incidents with 22, followed by Yala with 18 and Pattani with 11. Pattani recorded incidents in Chanae, Chanae Noi, Cho-airong, Chue-peng, Sungai Padi and Koh Chawi.

items.title: Alibaba proposes US$10bil share placement to fund global AI drive
items.summary: HONG KONG: Chinese tech giant Alibaba said on Sunday that it plans to issue HK$80 billion (US$10.2 billion) in new shares in Hong Kong to fund its global artificial intelligence ambitions. "The Equity Placement is being undertaken to extend the Company's global AI leadership," Alibaba said in a statement. Alibaba on Thursday announced nearly 269 billion yuan (US$40 billion) in revenue in its most recent quarter – a nine percent year-on-year increase – boosted by the global artificial intelligence frenzy driving demand for its products.

items.title: Robots can outrun humans, but can they plug in a cable?
items.summary: BEIJING: China's humanoid robots have shown they can run quicker than the fastest humans. The five-day World Humanoid Robot Games, which began Saturday in Beijing, combine events modelled on human sports with those designed to test the robots in simulated factories, restaurants, offices and in emergency situations. On Saturday, two robots ran faster than Usain Bolt's 9.58-second world record in the 100-metre sprint.

items.title: Rubber market to trade higher on strong demand
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian rubber market is expected to trade higher this week, supported by strong demand and concerns over supply constraints. The Malaysian Rubber Glove Manufacturers Association (Margma) said demand is expected to strengthen, particularly in China, which has pledged additional fiscal policy measures aimed at supporting economic growth. Industry expert Denis Low said the Malaysian rubber market is expected to trend slightly higher next week, supported by potential restocking demand from China and firmer crude oil prices.

items.title: PM approves additional RM1mil for Hindu crematorium project in Bagan - PHEB
items.summary: BUTTERWORTH: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has approved an additional RM1 million allocation to the Penang State Hindu Endowments Board (PHEB) for the construction of a modern Hindu crematorium in Bagan here, said PHEB chairman RSN Rayer. He said the additional allocation brought the total funding for the project to RM2.5 million, up from the RM1.5 million previously approved by Anwar. He said the original RM1.5 million allocation was found to be insufficient to implement the project, which is much needed by the Hindu community, particularly in Seberang Prai.

items.title: IIUM ends ties with academic behind controversial Roman-Malay shipbuilding claim
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 23 — International Islamic University Malaysia (IIUM) has confirmed that controversial academic Solehah Yaacob is no longer with the university, months after she drew public scrutiny over claims that ancient Romans learned shipbuilding from Malays and that meteor activity may explain Kedah’s iron ore deposits. The university said Solehah was also barred from using any official title, position or affiliation linking her to IIUM in promotional materials, media reports, publications, advertisements, social media content, publicity materials or other forms of public dissemination. IIUM said the clarification was necessary to prevent confusion over Solehah’s status and protect the university’s institutional integrity in academic representation.

items.title: CPO futures expected to stay bullish next week
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Crude palm oil (CPO) futures on Bursa Malaysia Derivatives are expected to trade with a bullish bias next week, supported by persistent weather concerns and Indonesia's B50 biodiesel programme. Ng expects CPO prices to trade between RM4,950 per tonne and RM5,100 per tonne next week. The December 2026 contract advanced RM198 to RM5,077 per tonne, January 2027 climbed RM182 to RM5,118 per tonne, and February 2027 increased RM167 to RM5,141 per tonne.

items.title: World Bank projects Lebanon economy to contract by 6.4pct due to war
items.summary: BEIRUT: The World Bank on Friday projected that Lebanon's economy would contract by 6.4 percent this year, as the latest Israel-Hezbollah war derailed the country's efforts at recovery. Due to the war, "real gross domestic product (GDP) is projected to contract by 6.4 per cent in 2026, reflecting the collapse in tourism, weaker consumption, disrupted supply chains, heightened insecurity, and prolonged displacement," the World Bank said in a report. The World Bank said Lebanon's economy had strengthened before the latest conflict, with an estimated real GDP growth of 4.2 per cent in 2025, "the fastest since the onset of the 2019 financial crisis."

items.title: Solehah Yaacob no longer with IIUM after Roman-Malay shipbuilding claim
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The International Islamic University Malaysia (IIUM) has clarified that controversial academic Dr Solehah Yaacob is no longer associated with the university after her service ended on April 27. Solehah had previously drawn attention over a series of controversial historical assertions. IIUM's Office for Communication, Advocacy and Promotion for Change (OCAP) said Solehah no longer held a position as a professor or represented the university in any capacity.

items.title: Major Japan defence firms stepping up drone development
items.summary: TOKYO: Major Japanese defence companies such as Mitsubishi Heavy Industries Ltd. are stepping up their development of drones as the government seeks to make unmanned systems and artificial intelligence a central part of its new defence strategy, Kyodo News reported. Mitsubishi Heavy said in May that it had developed a prototype interceptor drone capable of shooting down incoming attack drones. Mitsubishi Heavy plans to produce a variety of drones in small batches and continually revise their specifications, Ito said.

items.title: Sabah searchers find body of one boy after two teens swept away in Keningau river
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Aug 23 — A recreational outing turned tragic when a 16-year-old boy was found dead in Sungai Pegalan, Keningau today, while rescuers continue searching for his 13-year-old friend who was swept away by the strong current. Family members alerted police after learning that the boys were missing, prompting a search and rescue operation. A joint search and rescue team comprising seven police officers, nine firefighters and 13 APM personnel remains deployed at the scene in the search for Khend.

items.title: NCT, RHB move to strengthen SME growth ecosystem
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A strong business ecosystem is crucial to supporting Malaysia's small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) as the country advances its industrial transformation. NCT Group of Companies general manager of sales and marketing Simon Chan said SMEs remained an important engine of Malaysia's economic resilience. Chan was speaking in conjunction with NCT Group's partnership with RHB Bank Bhd and Syarikat Jaminan Pembiayaan Perniagaan Bhd to support SME growth through tailored financing solutions and government guarantee schemes.

items.title: Companies bank on stronger 2H as restructuring drives growth
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Companies are hoping for a stronger second half of the year as they move to turn restructuring efforts, new investments and strategic acquisitions into stronger revenue and profitability. Robo.ai Inc has outlined commercialisation, technology scaling and supply chain strengthening as key priorities for the second half of 2026, following a series of acquisitions, restructuring exercises and corporate transactions. The company said its overall direction and strategic moves are now fully synchronised, following a string of completed acquisitions, restructuring exercises and corporate transactions since the beginning of the year.

items.title: Dzulkefly: Haze drives sharp rise in asthma, respiratory infections
items.summary: KUALA SELANGOR: The Health Ministry has recorded a sharp surge in asthma and upper respiratory tract infection (URTI) cases as haze conditions affect several parts of the country. Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said monitoring between epidemiological weeks (EW) 32 and 33 showed asthma cases jumped by 259 per cent, while URTI cases rose by 124 per cent. "URTI recorded the highest number at 3,674 cases, up from 1,637, while asthma cases reached 219 compared with 61 previously.

items.title: Nearly 1,000 youths light up Kota Baru in Merdeka unity walk
items.summary: The inaugural Madani Glow Walk brought together youths from various backgrounds, including students from higher learning institutions, to mark Merdeka. Almost 500 participants registered within 10 days," he said. Ezzat said female participation was also strong, reflecting widespread interest among youths in celebrating National Day together.

items.title: Health Ministry reports surge in respiratory illnesses as several areas hit unhealthy API levels
items.summary: “URTI recorded the highest number at 3,674 cases, an increase from 1,637, while asthma cases reached 219 compared with 61 cases. Conjunctivitis cases, meanwhile, dropped to 146 from 157 cases,” he said. On heat-related illnesses, Dzulkefly said 90 cases had been recorded, comprising 71 cases of heat exhaustion, 14 heatstroke cases and five heat cramps cases.

items.title: Neighbourly row lands 80-year-old man in Penang Hospital, 62-year-old man in police custody
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 23 — A dispute between neighbours turned violent this morning when a 62-year-old man allegedly attacked his 80-year-old neighbour with a steel rod in Jalan Perak here. George Town district police chief Assistant Commissioner Abdul Rozak Muhammad said police received information about the incident at about 9.55am, with preliminary investigations indicating the assault happened about 9.30am outside the victim’s house, The Star reported. “The victim, an 80-year-old local man, was allegedly assaulted by his 62-year-old neighbour, who used a steel rod,” he was quoted as saying.

items.title: Police launch lockdown operation after ten migrants escape Tanah Merah Immigration Depot
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Aug 23 — Ten undocumented migrants escaped from the Tanah Merah Immigration Depot early this morning, police said. Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat said all the migrants were under the custody of the Kelantan Immigration Department and that police would conduct further investigations into the incident. We will investigate further,” he told a press conference at the Kelantan police contingent headquarters here.

items.title: 80-year-old man allegedly attacked with iron rod by neighbour
items.summary: Northeast district police chief Assistant Commissioner Abdul Rozak Muhammad said police received a report on the incident at 9.55am, following an altercation at 9.30am. "Initial investigations found that the victim was assaulted by his neighbour with an iron rod in front of the victim's house," he said. Abdul Rozak said the victim sustained serious injuries to his hands and legs and was receiving treatment at Penang Hospital.

items.title: BN conducting detailed study before deciding on Melaka election cooperation, says Zahid
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 23 — Barisan Nasional (BN) is conducting a detailed study on the possibility of cooperating with any political coalition in the upcoming Melaka state election, said its chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi. He said any decision on the matter would be made by the Melaka BN leadership and finalised at the central level. In the 2021 Melaka state election, BN won 21 of the 28 state seats, while Pakatan Harapan secured five seats and Perikatan Nasional two.

items.title: Forensic audit needed to determine abuse or governance lapses in Felda, says DPM Zahid
items.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said a management audit alone would be insufficient, given that issues involving the agency had persisted for a long time and resulted in losses amounting to billions of ringgit. “Felda is facing very serious and long-standing problems. Last Friday, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said he would await the full report of the Special Task Force investigating Felda’s management issues before making any official announcement.

items.title: 167,000 international students contribute RM20bil annually to Malaysia's economy – EMGS
items.summary: KUALA NERUS: The presence of about 167,000 international students in Malaysia currently contributes around RM20 billion annually to the country's economy through spending on tuition fees and living expenses, said Education Malaysia Global Services (EMGS) chief executive officer (CEO) Novie Tajuddin. He said Malaysia aims to attract 500,000 international students by 2035, as outlined in the 10-year Malaysia Higher Education Blueprint. "We currently have 167,000 international students.

items.title: Teen drowns, another missing in Sungai Pagalan incident
items.summary: KENINGAU: A 16-year-old boy drowned while another remains missing after they went swimming in Sungai Pagalan, near the Pagalan Ferry Jetty in Jalan Bakti Logam. Keningau Fire and Rescue station chief Senior Assistant Fire Superintendent Severinus Nidzam Sainkui said the second day of the search and rescue (SAR) operation resumed at 9am. "PPDA divers launched their first dive at 10.30am and located the victim four minutes later," he said in a statement.

items.title: GOF seizes RM1.135m in gold‑mining equipment in Kuala Betis raid; suspect allegedly misused sand‑extraction permit
items.summary: GUA MUSANG, Aug 23 — The General Operations Force (GOF) seized equipment worth RM1.135 million believed to have been used for illegal gold mining and arrested four men, including a Chinese national, in a raid at the Kuala Betis Resettlement Scheme (RPS) here yesterday. Southeast Brigade commander SAC Ahmad Radzi Hussain said the raid, conducted at about 4pm, was carried out by the brigade’s intelligence team under Ops Gali Mega (Eastern Zone). He said checks at the site uncovered two excavators, sluice boxes, suction machines, generator sets each, 51 pieces of grass carpet in various sizes and three rolls of grass carpet, all believed to have been used in the gold mining operation.

items.title: Civil defence man killed by king cobra had survived three snakebites
items.summary: TEMERLOH: Sergeant (PA) Muhamad Muazam Shah Kamardin had survived several venomous snakebites before a king cobra killed him during a demonstration yesterday, including one three years ago that left him in a coma. His sister, Siti Aisyah Kamardin, 43, said her brother, who was attached to the Temerloh Civil Defence Force, had been hospitalised three times after being bitten by venomous snakes. Muazam Shah, 39, died at Sultan Haji Ahmad Shah Hospital here at 1.50am today after being bitten by a king cobra during a demonstration at Taman Temerloh Jaya yesterday.

items.title: Japan earthquake injures dozens
items.summary: TOKYO: A magnitude 5.9 earthquake struck near Tokyo early Sunday, injuring at least 37 people and disrupting travel in the bustling megacity. The quake struck the southern part of Ibaraki Prefecture near Tokyo at 2am (1700 GMT on Saturday), the Japan Meteorological Agency said. Japan's Fire and Disaster Management Agency said at least 37 people had suffered minor injuries.

items.title: South Korean survivor fights for workplace harassment 'justice'
items.summary: Baek, 40, experienced first-hand a troubling paradigm in South Korea's workplace harassment response, with victims often expected to keep silent while employers have no clear legal duty to tell them how their cases ended. At her former company, a US firm with offices overseas, Baek said she was verbally harassed by her boss, an older man. The company still declined to disclose what disciplinary action had been taken, citing the need to "align with a privacy protection law" in South Korea, Baek said.

items.title: Teen girl fled motorcyclist after he allegedly told her to undress, Kelantan police now investigating possible sexual assault
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Aug 23 — Police are looking into a possible sexual offence involving a 15-year-old girl who was found unconscious by the roadside in Machang on August 20, after she allegedly fled from a man who told her to remove her clothes. Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat said the girl had run away from home before meeting the unidentified motorcyclist and accepting a ride from him, Harian Metro reported today. Mohd Yusoff said a medical examination found no evidence of rape, but police were concerned that an attempted sexual offence may have occurred.

items.title: Selangor, Federal govt agree on five measures to tackle Klang Valley floods
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Selangor and federal governments have agreed to implement five key measures to reduce flooding affecting Klang Valley residents. In a joint statement today following a meeting between Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh and Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari on flood retention ponds and crematoriums, both sides agreed to hold a technical meeting within two weeks. "Other measures include reviewing the capacity of Batu Dam and Klang Gate Dam, identifying locations for new flood retention ponds, increasing the capacity of three existing ponds, and coordinating river dredging and silt removal works," the statement said.

items.title: No Malaysians affected by simultaneous attacks in three southern Thai provinces, says Kelantan police chief
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Aug 23 — Kelantan Police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat said there is no report of Malaysians being affected by a series of simultaneous violent incidents in three provinces in southern Thailand last night. He said the advice was not new and had been conveyed several times to Malaysians planning to travel to southern Thailand. “I advised them not to enter Hat Yai as there were 51 incidents in three provinces in southern Thailand last night,” he said.

items.title: Sydney marathon unveils medal with wrong stadium
items.summary: SYDNEY: Organisers of the 2026 Sydney Marathon have sparked online mirth by unveiling a participation medal depicting a stadium in far-away Munich, Germany. The two-sided medal is engraved with a Sydney skyline showing course landmarks including the Opera House, the Sydney Harbour Bridge – and the Allianz Arena in Munich. Munich's Allianz Arena treated the medal muddle with good humour.

items.title: Zahid calls for trust to translate into votes, hints at 'Blue Wave' [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi today called for public trust to be translated into votes, as he quipped about a "Blue Wave" taking shape in the country. "Malaysia has built its leadership on trust. Our responsibility now is to turn that trust into stronger partnerships, trust into votes, trust into 'Blue Wave', a new wave happening in Malaysia.

items.title: GOF seizes RM304,000 worth of contraband cigarettes in Jenjarom
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The General Operations Force (GOF) seized 805 cartons of contraband cigarettes worth more than RM304,000 during a raid on a workers' quarters used as a syndicate storehouse in Kampung Sungai Rambai, Jenjarom, Selangor, two days ago. GOF 4th Battalion commanding officer Superintendent Amanjit Singh said the operation was carried out by a team of officers and personnel from the 4th Battalion GOF intelligence branch in Semenyih, with assistance from the Kuala Langat district police headquarters criminal investigation department. He said the premises, located within a lorry workshop compound, were rented by the syndicate to store illicit cigarettes.

items.title: Man dies after motorcycle hits fallen tree on Kuala Terengganu–Kota Bharu road in Setiu
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 23 — A permanent resident Indonesian man died after his motorcycle crashed into a fallen tree along Jalan Kampung Merang on the Kuala Terengganu–Kota Bharu coastal route late last night. Bernama reported that the victim, identified as 68‑year‑old construction worker Darman Khamis, was believed to be travelling from Kuala Terengganu towards Kampung Bari Besar when the crash occurred. Setiu district police chief Supt Zahril Asri Mohd Zain said police received information about the accident at about 12.10am from the Setiu district police traffic complaint counter.

items.title: Predawn robbery at Miri mini market leaves worker with injuries, police nab three Malaysian suspects
items.summary: MIRI, Aug 23 — A quiet early morning at a Tudan mini-market turned violent when three men allegedly broke into the premises, attacked an employee and fled with cash and other items. “The victim suffered injuries to her hand and shoulder before receiving treatment at Miri Hospital,” Miri district police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Farhan Lee Abdullah was quoted as saying. Police later arrested three Malaysian men aged between 28 and 39, acting on information received and conducting follow-up investigations.

items.title: Schools in 10 Sarawak districts to resume classes tomorrow as API improves
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 23 — All primary and secondary schools under the 10 District Education Offices (PPDs) in Sarawak will operate as usual from tomorrow, following improvements in Air Pollutant Index (API) readings. The Sarawak State Education Department (JPNS) said the schools under the PPDs of Kuching, Padawan, Bau, Lundu, Samarahan, Simunjan, Serian, Sri Aman, Lubok Antu and Betong would reopen as scheduled. JPNS reminded schools to take precautionary measures if haze affects their respective areas.

items.title: EMGS: International students generate RM20b a year for Malaysia’s economy, each contributing an estimated RM10,000 monthly
items.summary: KUALA NERUS, Aug 23 — The presence of about 167,000 international students in Malaysia currently contributes around RM20 billion annually to the country’s economy through spending on tuition fees and living expenses, said Education Malaysia Global Services (EMGS) chief executive officer (CEO) Novie Tajuddin. He said Malaysia aims to attract 500,000 international students by 2035, as outlined in the 10-year Malaysia Higher Education Blueprint. “We currently have 167,000 international students.

items.title: Allegedly struck with shoe and pencil case: Penang Education Dept steps in after 12-year-old cries assault by teacher in class
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 23 — The Penang Education Department has taken precautionary steps to protect a 12-year-old boy while investigating a complaint that he was allegedly assaulted by a teacher at a school in the Northeast district. The department said the teacher no longer has direct contact with the pupil, who has also been referred to the school’s Guidance and Counselling teacher for appropriate support and intervention, Harian Metro reported today. He said the Northeast Penang District Education Office was conducting the investigation and would take further action based on its findings.

items.title: Budget 2027: Social Welfare Dept requests increase in RM500 caregiver assistance for bedridden patients
items.summary: “We will bring this matter to the government and hope it will be considered,” he said after officiating the 2026 JKM Volunteer Convention here yesterday. Che Murad Sayang said JKM had also requested additional allocations to strengthen efforts to assist disadvantaged groups in society. He said information provided by volunteers on the ground helped JKM identify community needs in formulating policies and implementing welfare programmes.

items.title: Malaysia, Pakistan share diplomatic experiences in easing regional and global tensions
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 23 — Malaysia and Pakistan’s experiences in facilitating negotiations to resolve conflicts were among the matters discussed during a meeting between Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail and Pakistan’s Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir. The meeting with Syed Asim was held at the General Headquarters in Rawalpindi during Saifuddin Nasution’s official visit to Pakistan Saifuddin Nasution said the meeting provided an opportunity for both sides to exchange views on regional and international security developments, including diplomatic approaches and peace-building efforts in addressing conflicts and geopolitical tensions. During the meeting, Syed Asim shared Pakistan’s experience in facilitating peace talks.

items.title: KL Club VIP room turns into assault scene: Businessman charged after foreign woman alleges beating and gun threat
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 23 — A 36-year-old businessman has been charged with assaulting a 28-year-old foreign woman at a Kuala Lumpur club earlier this month, after the case drew renewed calls for police to reopen the investigation. Wangsa Maju district police chief Assistant Commissioner Annas Sulaiman said police referred the case to prosecutors on August 11, before the suspect was charged on August 13 under Section 323 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing hurt, The Star reported today. Annas said the victim lodged a police report on August 6, with the initial investigation conducted under Sections 323 and 506 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing hurt and criminal intimidation.

items.title: Bigger dams, more ponds, river dredging: KL and Selangor plan five flood fixes on the table
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 23 — Kuala Lumpur and Selangor are joining forces to tackle the Klang Valley’s flood problems, with plans to review dam capacity, build new retention ponds and dredge rivers as part of a five-point action plan. The move comes as both administrations seek to better manage water flowing from Hulu Selangor through Kuala Lumpur and towards the southern parts of the Klang Valley, where heavy rain can quickly turn into flooding. “Selangor and Kuala Lumpur must join forces to manage water drainage from the Hulu Selangor area which flows through Kuala Lumpur and onward to the southern localities,” Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari and Federal Territories Minister Hannah Yeoh said in a joint statement today.

items.title: Sabah records biggest unemployment drop as MYFutureJobs efforts yield over 71,000 job placements
items.summary: Chief Minister Datuk Seri Panglima Hajiji Noor said Sabah recorded the most significant reduction in unemployment among all states in Malaysia during the first quarter of this year. “This reflects the government’s continued commitment to helping Sabahans secure employment and improve their economic well-being,” he said in a speech read by Deputy Chief Minister II Datuk Seri Panglima Masidi Manjun during the launch of the MYFutureJobs X Oil & Gas Kota Kinabalu 2026 Career Carnival at the Sabah International Convention Centre (SICC) here yesterday. Khairul Firdaus said Kesuma was also implementing a paradigm shift to strengthen Sabah’s labour market through the Sabah Talent Development Centre (STDC), which serves as a strategic platform integrating talent development with industry requirements and labour market information.

items.title: Budget 2027 to focus on cost‑of‑living issues and attracting investment, says Fahmi
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 23 — The government will place greater emphasis on addressing the people’s cost-of-living issues more comprehensively in Budget 2027, taking into account the unsettled global geopolitical situation, said Madani Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. Fahmi, who is also Communications Minister, said the budget preparations would also consider various external factors, including movements in global crude oil prices. Also present was Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya Information Department director Normaizatulakmal Tujad.

items.title: Before the next tree falls, DBKL places 200 sensors to keep dangerous ones in check
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 23 — Kuala Lumpur is turning to technology to keep a closer watch on its ageing trees, with City Hall set to install at least 200 sensors that can flag potential hazards in real time. Kuala Lumpur mayor Datuk Seri Fadlun Mak Ujud said the sensors would be placed on selected mature trees about 1.2 metres above ground and linked to DBKL’s control centre, The Star r eported. The move forms the second phase of DBKL’s urban tree management programme after the city completed the mapping of 25,000 trees earlier this year with funding from the Digital Ministry.

items.title: Malaysian caught in Golok lockdown after bomb blasts stranded in Thai town
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Aug 23 — A Malaysian visitor to Sungai Golok in southern Thailand found himself caught in a night of chaos after a string of bomb blasts sent military and fire trucks onto the streets and triggered roadblocks across the border town. The visitor, identified only as Main, told The New Straits Times that key roads were closed by security personnel shortly after the explosions began. After hearing the first blast, Main spoke to residents who told him coordinated attacks were taking place at several locations across southern Thailand.

items.title: Man killed in car‑lorry collision along Bintulu-Samalaju Coastal Road
items.summary: BINTULU, Aug 23 — A man was killed after the car he was driving collided with a lorry along the Bintulu-Samalaju Coastal Road here yesterday. The Sarawak Fire and Rescue Department (Bomba), in a statement, said a team from the Kidurong Fire and Rescue Station was dispatched to the scene after receiving an emergency call about the accident at around 8.41am. “Upon arriving at the scene, the firefighters found that an accident involving a car and a lorry had occurred,” it said in a statement.
